optimizedDescription.value: Canonical spec ID `workspace:capabilityPath`; bare path → default; reject unknown workspace and Windows device segments.

optimizedContext.value:
# Spec ID Format

## Rules
- Format: `workspace:capabilityPath` (colon sep; all `/` in path). Single format everywhere: storage (`change.specIds`, manifest), domain refs, CLI input, metadata `dependsOn`, user output. No internal vs external split.
- No colon → workspace `default`, whole string = capability path. `auth/login` → `default:auth/login`.
- Unknown workspace (colon-qualified) → reject.
- Parse: first `:` → workspace + path (validate workspace exists); else default + full string. `/` never workspace separator.
- Capability-path segment that is Windows device name MUST reject on every OS. Reserved (case-insensitive, whole segment): `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1` through `com9`, `lpt1` through `lpt9`. Segment `con-foo` legal. Windows drive letter is not a workspace; spec IDs are not filesystem paths.
- Acceptors SHOULD normalize bare paths to fully-qualified (`default:capPath`) at system boundary. Domain MAY assume already qualified.
- `specDependsOn` MUST use fully-qualified IDs (`workspace:capabilityPath`). Bare paths in metadata MUST normalize before storage.

## Constraints
- Workspace names MUST NOT contain `/` or `:`.
- Capability paths MUST NOT contain `:`.
- Separator always `:` — `/` never workspace separator.
- Default workspace implicit when no colon present.
